title: Wigland - where dairying meets sheep country - geograph.org.uk - 130888
author: Mike Harris
description: Wigland - where dairying meets sheep country. View from Wigland footpath 3 on bearing of 200 deg. This is a dairy farm that also collects old tyres - like all too many in Cheshire. The valley in mid-field belongs to a tributary stream to Wych Brook - the end of Scholar's Wood just enters the image from the right. The undulating and somewhat wooded scenery, cut by quite steep-sided stream valleys, is typical of the area in the extreme south of west Cheshire alongside the Welsh border ... very different from the much flatter main part of the Cheshire plain further north. Although Wigland Farm seems to concentrate on dairying, many of the farms around here focus more on sheep.

title: Wych Brook Valley - geograph.org.uk - 130895
author: Mike Harris
description: Wych Brook Valley. View across the valley of Wych Brook on bearing of 255 deg from Wigland footpath 8, just south of its junction with footpath 5. The foreground is in England (and SJ 4943), beyond the valley is Wales (and SJ 4843) with Pen-y-Bryn Farm on the skyline. Wych Brook itself - invisible in its deep valley in midfield - only the tree tops showing - forms the border between Cheshire and Wales. This undulating terrain is mostly sheep farming country.
